correctness.rationale: A positive-column-diagonally-dominant M-matrix gives the unique stable steady state. Cofactor inversion yields three exact rational exported fractions. The middle derivative is a quadratic whose three coefficient sign thresholds are strictly ordered by comparing upstream and downstream removal rates. Opposite leading/constant signs give precisely one positive root; outside the interval every nonzero coefficient has a common sign. Upstream and downstream derivative coefficients are strictly signed, and two-box gradients have fixed sign. A standard-library rational linear-system checker passed 25,248 exact-arithmetic assertions; no finite testing is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A natural directed three-compartment water balance is the smallest chain where the steady export fraction can have an interior dispersive optimum. The source-specific and rate-specific global classification decides whether exchange is always helpful/harmful for downstream pollution or creates a unique best/worst mixing rate. A rational example has an exactly verified 9.09% increase at its worst rate, while another simple integer example has a 40.9% increase, so the threshold is not merely a tiny numerical perturbation. Useful as a sharp benchmark for reactive transport and screening assumptions about monotonic impact of dispersion; no field-scale forecast is claimed.
